questions.question_text: How many straws are needed for a triangular-prism frame?

options.why: Counts the vertices instead of the edges.
Counts the faces instead of the edges.
Counts each triangular base as $6$ edges, then adds the $3$ joining edges: $6+6+3=15$.

questions.solution_text: Two triangular bases give $6$ edges and three joining edges give $9$.

questions.question_text: How many joiners are needed for a square-pyramid frame?

options.why: Counts only the base vertices and omits the apex.
Counts the edges instead of the vertices.
Adds two apex joiners instead of one.

questions.solution_text: There are four base vertices and one apex, so $5$ joiners are needed.

questions.question_text: Which face set builds a pentagonal prism?

options.why: Keeps both bases but makes the side faces triangles, as in a pyramid, instead of rectangles.
Counts only the bottom base and forgets the matching pentagon on top.
Makes both slips at once and so gives the faces of a pentagonal pyramid, not a prism.

questions.solution_text: A pentagonal prism has two pentagonal bases and one rectangle for each base side.

questions.question_text: Which face set builds a triangular pyramid?

options.why: Gives the faces of a triangular prism.
Uses rectangular side faces as though building a prism.

questions.solution_text: A triangular pyramid has one triangular base and three triangular side faces.

questions.question_text:
A prism frame has $15$ edges.
What is its base shape?

options.why: Divides the edge count by $5$ instead of by $3$.
Counts one more base side than the edge structure allows.
Uses all $15$ frame edges as if they belonged to one base instead of separating base and joining edges.

questions.solution_text: A prism with an $n$-sided base has $3n$ edges, and $15\div3=5$.

questions.question_text:
A square-pyramid model has the correct five vertices but only seven edges.
What must be added?

options.why: The model already has the correct four base vertices and apex.
A skeletal model is missing a straw edge, not a solid face.
Adds too many edges; a complete square pyramid needs eight.

questions.solution_text: A square pyramid needs $8$ edges, so a seven-edge frame is missing one.
